newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Fin Min sceptical on Moody's Bulgaria debt rating.
newsitem.headline: Fin Min sceptical on Moody's Bulgaria debt rating.

text.p: Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said on Saturday the ratings assigned to Bulgaria by Moody's Investors Service had no serious weight as the country did not currently plan to place issues on global markets.

Moody's assigned two weeks ago sovereign ceilings of B3 for ratings of foreign currency bonds and notes, Caa for ratings of foreign currency-denominated long-term bank deposits and Not Prime for ratings for short-term obligations of issuers domiciled in Bulgaria.
"We did not request the rating. We are not launching a bond issue on international markets," Kostov told reporters on arrival from the annual IMF/World Bank meeting in Washington.
Moody's assigned B3 ratings to some $5 billion worth of Bulgarian Brady bonds issued as part of an $8.16 billion foreign commercial debt restructuring deal in 1994.
"The rating in itself has no outstanding significance as the value of Bulgarian debt was seen in the price of the Brady Bonds on international markets," he added.
"In the future the government will have to launch issues on international markets, but then we will request ratings from several agencies," said Kostov.

The Bulgarian Bradies, which consist of Discount Bonds, Front-Loaded Interest Bonds and Interest Arrears Bonds, eased recently as the International Monetary Fund has twice delayed funding until the government stabilised the crumbling economy.
